status: FROZEN: implementation, isolated tests and independent final review complete
scope: Managed Crowd Control only. No live game, Twitch/network actions, native changes, UI/build/version/coverage edits or full build.
api: EffectDefinition.ActiveCheck: optional read-only ongoing usability predicate, separate from Check and ControlReadiness. Cleanup does not invoke it. Internal EffectContext.ReadRestorableValue returns only a finite observation accepted by FeatureMap/FeatureDefinition.IsValidValue; no duplicate range constants.
changes: Unlimited MP requires current integer MP maximum 1..255 and both MP capabilities while running. Missing, nonfinite, fractional, negative, greater-than-255 and zero observations pause usefulness.

ActiveCheck gates timer accounting, established monitors, sustain and paid extensions. Both endpoint samples must be usable; resource-conditioned intervals over one second charge zero even if control timer pausing is disabled.
Returning MP availability triggers immediate sustain without retroactive time charge. Extensions wait unpaid until useful. Control pause opt-out otherwise preserves existing wall-time semantics.
Cleanup retains control, role, finite owned-toggle readback and value comparison gates. Gauge loss does not block a zero write; rejected restores remain deferred and recover without an MP gauge.
MP-only start checks reject actual zero but wait for malformed or unavailable maxima.

Movement rewards retain Sora-only admission. Required originals must be finite, available and accepted by their FeatureDefinition edit bounds before the first write; missing or out-of-policy second originals after the first awaited write trigger existing partial failure cleanup. No defaults 8/2/160 are guessed.

Movement ActiveCheck also pauses runtime use while originals are missing or outside policy. SustainAsync validates each restoring live original against its own FeatureDefinition immediately before writing, preserving a non-restorable external value even if it appears during an earlier awaited command. Non-restoring values keep their existing sustain semantics.
Moon Jump describes increased base jump height and capped falling speed; gravity is unchanged and High Jump/special actions may use other values.

nativeReference.rule: Integer STATUS+388 is bounded to 0..255; positive values identify a usable MP gauge.

cases: All three audited roles and supported-role transitions with missing/NaN/infinite/negative/fractional/out-of-byte-range/zero MP maxima.
Integer usable endpoints 1 and 255, capability loss/recovery, immediate recovery sustain and queued extensions.
Deferred cleanup across unsupported role/menu, refused restore, absent toggle readback, absent gauge, external toggle change and StopAll.
General timer pause opt-out, conservative long gaps, backward clock, ordinary effects without ActiveCheck, established monitor pause.

Movement role guards; missing/nonfinite/out-of-policy originals (walk100/run100/jump1200/fall0); exact per-feature minimum and maximum; missing or out-of-policy second original after first command; exact originals restored and writes clamped by the same catalog.

Script-set runtime run100/walk100/jump1200/fall0 pause duration/sustain; valid recovery stores a restorable original; ending preserves external values. A second out-of-policy value appearing during the first awaited sustain write is never overwritten or captured. Restore=false behavior remains unchanged.
Test-only permissive role definition reproduces equal-value replacement retaining the old Sora original; production catalog remains restricted.

remainingLimits: Readiness is sampled, not a native cumulative useful-time counter. A pause entirely between two observations cannot be reconstructed. Native command guards still decide at dispatch.
ActiveCheck proves current resource observations, not that every ongoing native refill executed; native dispatch can refuse when deeper resources are unavailable.

OwnedValue has no Actor lifetime token. If another Actor has the same applied movement value, it retains the old original. Sora-only admission avoids writing to newly admitted roles but does not prove identity across two Sora actor lifetimes.

Actor identity and observations can change after a host sample. This change adds startup, ongoing sampled and per-owned-value restore-range checks; it does not add an atomic actor-bound multi-field operation or an actor-lifetime token.
Deferred cleanup remains in memory and needs later ticks; it cannot survive trainer shutdown.

review.scope: Final MP and Movement startup/runtime restore-range logic independently reviewed, including the per-value await-race guard. No blocking finding. Reviewer independently read the 1687/0 author log; no duplicate build. Actor-lifetime limitation remains explicit.
